slot.brief: Match functional-group detection (Lassaigne's test: N, S, halogen) with correct observation/chemistry.

stem:
Match each element detected in Lassaigne's analysis with its characteristic positive result.

**List-I**
(P) Nitrogen
(Q) Sulphur
(R) Phosphorus
(S) Bromine

**List-II**
(1) Violet colour with sodium nitroprusside
(2) Pale-yellow $\text{AgBr}$ precipitate, soluble in concentrated $\text{NH}_3$
(3) Prussian blue colour after treatment with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and acidification
(4) Yellow precipitate with ammonium molybdate after oxidation

verdicts.working: Nitrogen gives Prussian blue (3); sulphur gives violet with sodium nitroprusside (1); phosphorus gives yellow ammonium molybdate precipitate (4); bromine gives pale-yellow AgBr (2).

working:
Nitrogen: $\text{CN}^-$ gives Prussian blue with $\text{FeSO}_4$ after acidification $\to$ (3).
Sulphur: $\text{S}^{2-}$ gives violet colour with sodium nitroprusside $\to$ (1).
Phosphorus: oxidised to phosphate; ammonium molybdate gives yellow precipitate $\to$ (4).
Bromine: $\text{Br}^-$ gives pale-yellow $\text{AgBr}$, soluble in concentrated $\text{NH}_3$ $\to$ (2).

Independent check: Nitrogen gives Prussian blue (3); sulphur gives violet with sodium nitroprusside (1); phosphorus gives yellow ammonium molybdate precipitate (4); bromine gives pale-yellow AgBr (2).
